target.title: fix: keep MCP Apps aligned with runtime tool policy
target.body:
Related: #69039

AI-assisted: implementation and review were performed with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where MCP App previews could disappear when optional resource listing failed, App-only tools could escape the originating run's effective tool policy, repeated preview-read failures could pause normal MCP calls, applied sandbox CSP was not advertised to the App, and Apps listener changes appeared hot-reloadable even though they require a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows up on the review feedback from #69039. It evaluates the complete MCP tool catalog, including App-only tools, through the same runtime and layered policy pipeline as model-visible tools; keeps optional preview discovery outside server-failure backoff; advertises the CSP actually applied by the host; and classifies `mcp.apps` listener changes as restart-required. Sandbox parent authentication is intentionally outside this follow-up.

## User Impact

MCP Apps remain available when servers omit or fail optional listing, App calls cannot exceed the tool policy of the run that opened the view, preview failures no longer disable unrelated MCP calls, Apps receive accurate CSP capabilities, and listener configuration changes take effect predictably after restart.

## Evidence

- Focused hosted tests: 538 assertions passed across MCP runtime, materialization, policy, Gateway, reload, and Control UI coverage.
- Regression follow-up: 99 focused assertions passed after adding complete-catalog App policy evaluation.
- Full changed-surface gate: `check:changed` passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxaddh6pywtjwvhcd9yhpecj` (core/UI/test-root typechecks, format, lint, and architecture guards).
- Package proof: OpenClaw and Control UI builds passed; npm tarball integrity passed.
- Live functional proof: `test:docker:agent-bundle-mcp-tools` passed from the packed artifact against a real stdio MCP server, including tool discovery, resource read, MCP App preview creation, profile filtering, and provider-bound tool serialization.
- Fresh pre-ship autoreview: no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: improve(ui): unify the New session draft with the start-screen layout
target.body:
Closes #105068

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the Control UI shows the chat start screen — hero, recent chats, composer. Clicking "New session" in the sidebar opens `/new`, which was a differently shaped page: bordered target chips stacked over a top-anchored composer, with the recent-chats list in a different position. The two "start working" surfaces looked unrelated.

## Why This Change Was Made

There should be one start-screen layout. The `/new` draft page now renders the exact same welcome block as the empty-chat start screen, with the draft controls folded into it launcher-style: hero on top, then a quiet one-line target row (agent, node, folder, worktree) directly above the composer in the middle of the pane, then the recent chats below.

- `new-session-page.ts` drops its private hero/recents copies and reuses `renderWelcomeState` from `chat-welcome.ts` via a new `composer` slot (rendered between the hero and the recents), so the two surfaces cannot drift apart; the now single-consumer welcome helpers are un-exported.
- The target controls lose their chip borders and become a muted text row (hover/focus restores contrast) in the spirit of Cursor's folder/branch/machine bar; the folder input hugs its content (`field-sizing: content` where supported, fixed fallback elsewhere) so the browse button sits next to the path.
- The app shell treats `new-session` as a chat-like route (`content--chat`/`shell--chat`): the pane owns its scrolling, the welcome centers vertically, and the scroll container's top inset doubles as the native macOS titlebar drag band via `beginNativeWindowDragFromTopInset`, mirroring the chat thread.
- Draft-session semantics are unchanged: same controls, same `sessions.create` payload, same redirect into the created chat.

## User Impact

The start screen and New Session now read as one screen: same hero, same recent-chats list, and on `/new` a clean "where does this session run" row directly above the composer. Works across desktop and mobile widths.

Desktop:

![desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/new-session-unified-start/new-session-unified-desktop.png)

Worktree fields expanded (custom folder forces a managed worktree):

![worktree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/new-session-unified-start/new-session-unified-worktree.png)

Mobile:

![mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/new-session-unified-start/new-session-unified-mobile.png)

## Evidence

- Live-verified against the mock dev harness (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`): `/new` desktop + mobile, folder browser opening below the target row, custom folder forcing the worktree toggle with base-branch/name fields wrapping into the quiet row, and the empty-chat start screen still rendering the shared welcome unchanged. Screenshots above.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/app/app-host.test.ts ui/src/app-navigation.test.ts ui/src/pages/new-session/create-params.test.ts` — all passing (235 tests; re-run after each iteration).
- Updated `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.e2e.test.ts`: the old `getByRole("heading", { name: "New session" })` wait was stale (that h1 was removed in #104819); it now waits for the hero heading and asserts hero → target row → composer ordering inside the welcome.
- Second-model review (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh) ran on the intermediate bottom-dock layout and came back clean after one accepted fix; re-run on the final centered layout before landing.
- No i18n changes (all strings already exist; `newSession.title` remains in use by the command palette and navigation copy).

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses. Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

This upgrades both hooks from fire-and-forget (void) to sequential modifying hooks. Replaces the closed #61485 with a clean implementation against current `main`.

- `llm_input` handlers can now return `{ block, blockReason, prompt, systemPrompt }` to block or modify the LLM call
- `llm_output` handlers can now return `{ assistantTexts }` to replace the model response (e.g. for redaction)
- Handlers returning `void` behave identically to before (fully backward compatible)

## User Impact

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override what's sent to the model
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the response (e.g. PII redaction)
- Existing plugins that return `void` are unaffected — fully backward compatible
- `allowPromptInjection=false` strips prompt/systemPrompt overrides but preserves block/blockReason

### Mutation semantics

**llm_input:**
- `prompt` / `systemPrompt`: first-setter-wins across priority-ordered handlers
- `block` / `blockReason`: sticky-true (any handler blocks; `shouldStop` exits early)
- Subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy — prompt fields stripped when `false`
- `evolveEvent` propagates the **accumulated merged result** to lower-priority handlers and resets `imagesCount` to 0
- `systemPrompt` override applied to active model session via `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt`

**llm_output:**
- `assistantTexts`: last-setter-wins with evolved event propagation
- Later hooks see prior modifications, preventing silent overwrites of higher-priority redactions

### Security boundaries

- `PluginBlockedError` sentinel skips failover/retry classification (not a transient provider failure)
- `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` strips `prompt`/`systemPrompt` from results when `allowPromptInjection=false`
- `historyMessages` deep-cloned via `cloneHookMessages` before passing to hooks
- `lastAssistant` deep-cloned via `structuredClone` before passing to `llm_output` hooks

### Cross-runner contract

- Embedded runner: fully consumes modifying results (block, prompt/systemPrompt override, output replacement)
- Harness helpers (`runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook`): upgraded from `void` to `Promise<Result | undefined>` so CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runners can consume modifying results
- Backward compatible — existing fire-and-forget callers discard the promise

### Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` | Add `PluginHookLlmInputResult`, `PluginHookLlmOutputResult` types with documented mutation semantics; add `llm_input` to prompt injection hook names; update handler map signatures |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | Add `evolveEvent` to `ModifyingHookPolicy`; wire into `runModifyingHook` using accumulated result; upgrade `runLlmInput`/`runLlmOutput` from `runVoidHook` to `runModifyingHook` |
| `src/plugins/registry.ts` | Add `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook`; handle `llm_input` in prompt injection guard |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Add `PluginBlockedError`; await `llm_input`/`llm_output` results; apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides to active session; wire output replacement |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Import `PluginBlockedError`; handle with `hook_block` error kind, skip failover |
| `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts` | Upgrade `runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook` to return `Promise<Result>` |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` | 18 unit tests: block, override, priority merge, A>B>C accumulated-result evolution, backward compat, error handling |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts` | 6 e2e tests: full plugin lifecycle from `api.on()` -> loader -> registry -> runner -> result |

## Evidence

### E2E plugin lifecycle proof (6 tests)

Exercises the full path from plugin `api.on()` registration through loader, registry, hook runner, to result consumption:

1. **Block**: Plugin returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "Content policy violation" }` when prompt contains "BLOCKED" — runner returns block result
2. **Prompt rewrite**: Plugin returns `{ prompt: "[SANITIZED] " + event.prompt }` — runner returns rewritten prompt
3. **System prompt override**: Plugin returns `{ systemPrompt: "compliance prompt" }` — runner returns override
4. **Output redaction**: Plugin replaces `secret` with `[REDACTED]` in `assistantTexts` via `llm_output` — runner returns redacted output
5. **Backward compat**: Plugin returns `void` from both hooks — runner returns `undefined` (no modification)
6. **allowPromptInjection=false**: Plugin returns block + prompt + systemPrompt — constraint strips prompt/systemPrompt, preserves block

### Unit tests (18 tests)

Cover hook merger internals: merge policy, evolveEvent, imagesCount reset, error handling, empty array suppression.

### Verification commands

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts  # 6/6 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts      # 18/18 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm.test.ts                # 5/5 pass (backward compat)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions                                          # typecheck clean
```

## ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed

All 3 findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103959#issuecomment-4939779091) fixed:

1. **evolveEvent uses accumulated result** — `hooks.ts`: `evolveEvent(event, result)` not `evolveEvent(event, handlerResult)`. A>B>C priority test validates.
2. **systemPrompt applied to active session** — `attempt.ts`: `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt()` called after hook override.
3. **Harness helpers return results** — `lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts`: both return `Promise<Result | undefined>` for cross-runner consumption.

## Supersedes

Replaces #61485 (closed by maintainer as stale)

target.title: refactor(agents): compress model prompts and tool instructions
target.body:
Closes #104996

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw repeats important operating rules in verbose system-prompt and built-in tool prose. That spends context tokens every turn and can bury the exact safety, routing, and scheduling invariants the model must follow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rewrite the core system prompt, GPT-5 overlays, subagent prompt, and OpenClaw-owned built-in tool descriptions as short imperative clauses. Preserve the behavioral contracts for approvals, external actions, message delivery, Gateway control, skills, ACP, and classic/event cron jobs; leave runtime logic, tool schema shapes, config, protocol, and provider/plugin-owned descriptions unchanged.

The exported GPT-5 overlay constants intentionally change value, so the generated Plugin SDK API hash is refreshed. Prompt snapshots and targeted assertions now protect the compact wording's semantic invariants instead of the retired prose.

## User Impact

Agents receive the same operating constraints with less repeated prompt overhead. A representative full system prompt drops from 10,849 to 6,982 characters (35.6%); rendered dynamic built-in tool catalogs drop 5.8-6.0% across Telegram, Discord, and heartbeat fixtures.

## Evidence

- Source-blind live GPT-5.6 Sol behavior contract: 10/10 scenarios passed against the rendered prompt and dynamic tool catalog, including timezone-preserving daily cron, five-minute stateful event cron, quiet false events, agent-turn launch on true events, message-tool-only replies, safe Gateway inspection, public-upload consent, and ACP available/unavailable routing.
- Prompt snapshots: 7/7 current on exact branch content.
- Gateway tool-resolution regression: 32/32 passed across gateway core, server, client, and methods projects.
- Exact-head changed gate: formatting, prompt snapshots, Plugin SDK API baseline, three tsgo lanes, core/script oxlint, import-cycle checks, and runtime guards passed on Testbox `tbx_01kxagzm23vazyddmyvgjahqcv` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29183050075)).
- Hosted PR CI exposed additional stale exact-prose assertions; all were retargeted to compact semantic contracts. Focused fallback proof passed 309 tests, and the CLI prompt suites passed 80/80 on Testbox ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29184791433)); full hosted PR CI remains the merge gate.
- Fresh autoreview: one valid stale negative assertion was fixed; the final rerun after CLI assertion cleanup reported no accepted/actionable findings. Earlier review findings around skill paths, task-name casing, consent, external messaging, and Control UI URL constraints were incorporated before this PR.

No agent transcript attached; validation results are summarized above.
